title: Calibrate fixed-prefix information against independent donor cohorts before claiming specificity
statement: The predeclared low fixed-prefix information cutoff plus at least four negative slopes passes all five held authors at 30,000 tokens. The same criterion passes 1/96 uniform banks, 20/96 length-conditioned banks, 88/96 independently generated length-and-count banks, and 86/96 books with latent bank switching. All donor fit words, input type frequencies and cohort parameters precede and exclude held authors. Monoalphabetic relabeling and whole-word order permutation preserve the results; within-word reversal also passes 5/5, and the reversible suffix-keyed shift of the first two letters passes 0/5. An added external-cohort diagnostic gives 96/96 passes when initials are inherited from the donor and 94/96 when donor word endings become initial groups of the synthetic forms. All 120 within-language comparisons of a terminal-cohort book to a held author give a lower score for the artificial book, by .521–1.006 bits. The four simpler bank families each score above the corresponding held books in all 936 supported repeated comparisons across size and smoothing. The prespecified uniform-bank gate still misclassifies many structured outputs. The studies constrain the specificity of this metric on these controls.
check: Compare independent candidate generators and well-supported historical languages before proposing any lexical-origin claim. Freeze training source, normalization, exact metric, separate calibration distribution and all decoding controls. Include both initial and terminal placement of constrained weights, stronger historical baselines, and a measurement that can detect order or context. Obtain the complete original methods or source implementation before calling any version an exact reproduction, and seek review of a declarative primitive before closed scoring.

method.target: Five suitable new-to-task works, by Boccaccio, Caesar, Gower, Juan Manuel and Malory, with bounded words. Four separate training works, by Dante, Augustine, Chaucer and Juan Ruiz, fit the corresponding donor language. Both English targets share a donor and cut. Full metadata, open source byte hashes and extraction script are provided.
method.metric: For total N, type count c and two-character prefix count C, use log2((N-c+alpha)/(C-c+alpha)). Compute a type mean and slope against log2(c/N) in each length bin 4–8; all types of length >=2 contribute prefix mass. The joint score is the equal mean of the five supported type means. The final measure is a fixed-prefix alternative.
method.calibration: At alpha=1 and 30,000 tokens, take the fifth order statistic of 99 independent donor uniform books per language; a joint score strictly below this threshold and at least four negative slopes pass the exploratory rule. Run 24 fresh synthetic draws per donor and per mechanism, plus supported 15,000/60,000 windows and alpha .5/2 as descriptive sensitivities. Keep the threshold fixed. Counts are conditional on these training works and priors.
method.banks: Fit length and coarse-count group prefix priors using only donor training types. Assign fresh artificial spelling maps and draw from the donor weight vector. Latent switching uses fresh lexicon seeds and samples more often from a randomly selected prefix bucket on blocks of 300 tokens. Compare separately the late-added exact initial and reverse-terminal cohort transfer with independent draws; the training cohort/count assignments are fixed, but generated sample frequencies vary.
method.cipher: Round-trip the monoalphabetic substitution, per-word reversal and suffix-dependent shift of the first two letters. Complete word order permutation is an additional invariant because types and counts are unchanged. The suffix shift is a mathematical stress control, not a suggested medieval practice.
method.endpoint: The 2020 published leave-one-out ratio has zero numerator at the uniqueness point. The publication gives no finite terminal convention and a public implementation was not located. In the supplemental replay, keep separate bounded and unbounded uniqueness, the finite preceding-segment mean, and the add-one including-terminal mean. The latter telescopes exactly to log2(N-c+1)/u. The formula audit reimplements the inherited fixed two-character score directly.

limits: The primary gate controls the declared uniform synthetic process only. Synthetic pass rates are descriptive per donor, with fresh seeds and common training weights. Matching exact donor cohorts can transfer genuine lexical properties into a stream with no authorial order or semantics. Lower values do not establish equivalent slope magnitudes. Historical work diversity is limited and Caesar is classical, while modern edited digital witnesses have different preparation. Caesar retains 2,087 v instances at baseline; applying the donor Latin v-to-u normalizer is a separate matching control and leaves the five cipher/control gate outcomes for Caesar unchanged. The study uses no manuscript evaluation.

editions.preprocessing: Casefold, transliterate œ/æ/þ/ð/ȝ, NFKD, remove combining marks, then maximal contiguous ASCII a–z runs. UTF-8, one space between tokens and final LF.

Use sample suffixes uniformly; for length2 no freely assignable stem independently of injectivity.
frozen_primary.latent_process: Reuse the training count-conditioned generator with a fresh independent lexicon. In each 300-token block select a latent four-way prefix bucket uniformly; 0.25 of draws use that group, remaining draws use all words. Both distributions derive from training.
frozen_primary.cipher_controls: Verify exact inverse for monoalphabetic, within-word reversal and SHA-256 suffix-keyed shift of first two characters. These preserve token boundaries, lengths, and full frequency counts. No noise or actual manuscript input.
frozen_primary.evaluation_sources: New distinct historic works under reads manifest; each must have >=30000 normalized words and author absent from all model fitting and P-J-028/027 fixed-prefix evaluations. Exact source, word limits and hashes fixed before reading any metric output.
frozen_primary.uncertainty: Report independent works individually and in work-level summaries. Repeated generator seeds are simulation variation conditional on their fixed training source. Unsupported cases shown explicitly.
clarifications_before_results: The five primary authors were selected by new-to-task status, >=30,000 bounded words and same-language donor availability.
The artificial symbol alphabet is the ASCII letter inventory observed in that language training sample.
The packet-free supplemental controls contain a whole-token permutation with the exact same dictionary and frequencies.
Compute the slope as the difference between numerator and competing-prefix log slopes for interpretation.
The 99 uniform calibrations are based on independent seeds. The first five joint tail scores set one predeclared cutoff for each training source; no held author is used.

supplemental_cohort_plan.role: Post-primary mechanistic diagnostic with unchanged main threshold
supplemental_cohort_plan.inputs: The same four separate author training samples, with no held work frequency information used for generation
mechanisms: Preserve exactly the training two-letter initial cohorts and per-type sampling weights, replace cohort symbols by a bijection and use fresh random bounded suffixes
Use the final two training letters read in reverse as the same artificial initial cohort key, after which the identical generation process applies
supplemental_cohort_plan.primary_reuse: Use unchanged cutoffs and supported-bin rule to score the supplemental samples. Compare actual held-work joint scores as a descriptive ranking only, with no new cutoff.

disclosed_seed_correction.mistake: Initial code reused exactly the same lexicon for the length-and-frequency and latent arms, although the frozen plan stipulated the latent arm should generate a fresh dictionary.
disclosed_seed_correction.correction: Use a distinct fixed XOR seed convention for the latent lexicon. The bank form, token seed, score, gate, other generator arms, calibration and held works remain identical by exact comparison.

scripts.cohort_replay.py:
"""Transfer exact training lexical cohorts to fresh artificial vocabularies."""
import argparse
from collections import Counter
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random

from prefix_bench import fit, LANGUAGE, Sampler, metric, decision, random_word

MODES=('initial_cohort','terminal_cohort')

def plant(train, mode, seed, n=30000):
    rng=random.Random(seed ^ 0x86A7B1FF)
    token_rng=random.Random(seed ^ 0xCA86E23A)
    abc=train['alphabet']
    replacement=list(abc)
    rng.shuffle(replacement)
    translate=str.maketrans(abc,''.join(replacement))
    seen=set()
    book={}
    for source,count in sorted(train['counts'].items()):
        represented=source if mode=='initial_cohort' else source[::-1]
        key=represented[:2].translate(translate)
        length=len(source)
        if length<=2:
            target=key
        else:
            for attempt in range(10000):
                target=key+random_word(rng,length-2,abc)
                if target not in seen:
                    break
            else:
                raise ValueError('Artificial cohort exceeds its supported suffix vocabulary')
        assert target not in seen
        seen.add(target)
        book[target]=count
    original_counts=Counter()
    for w,c in train['counts'].items():
        pattern=w if mode=='initial_cohort' else w[::-1]
        if len(w)>=2:
            original_counts[pattern[:2].translate(translate)]+=c
    artificial_counts=Counter()
    for w,c in book.items():
        if len(w)>=2:
            artificial_counts[w[:2]]+=c
    assert original_counts==artificial_counts
    assert sorted(book.values())==sorted(train['counts'].values())
    sample=Sampler(book.keys(),book.values())
    return sample.take(token_rng,n), len(book), len(original_counts)

def main():
    cli=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    cli.add_argument('raw',type=Path)
    cli.add_argument('primary',type=Path)
    ns=cli.parse_args()
    baseline=json.loads(ns.primary.read_text())
    results={}
    for i,(lang,preexisting) in enumerate(sorted(baseline['calibration'].items())):
        tref=fit(ns.raw,lang)
        cutoff=preexisting['threshold']
        results[lang]={}
        targets={w:baseline['works'][w]['30000']['plain']['1']['joint_score']
                 for w,meta in baseline['inputs'].items() if LANGUAGE[meta['language']]==lang}
        for mode in MODES:
            profile=[]
            for seed in range(880101,880125):
                sample,types,groups=plant(tref,mode,seed+1183*i)
                outcome=metric(sample)
                profile.append(dict(seed=seed+1183*i,types=types,cohorts=groups,equality_checked=True,
                    outcome=outcome,gate=decision(outcome,cutoff),
                    score_below_held_works={w:outcome['joint_score']<=v for w,v in targets.items()}))
            results[lang][mode]=profile
    print(json.dumps(results,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':
    main()

"""Replay the inherited formula with an independent implementation."""
import argparse
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import json
from math import log2
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean
from vs.refcorpus import normalize
from prefix_bench import LENGTHS, compare

def prior_formula(tokens,alpha):
    freq=Counter(tokens)
    n=len(tokens)
    cohorts=defaultdict(list)
    for w,v in freq.items():
        if len(w)>=2:
            cohorts[w[:2]].append((w,v))
    classes={}
    for length in LENGTHS:
        pairs=[]
        for w,v in freq.items():
            if len(w)!=length:
                continue
            competitor=sum(c for q,c in cohorts[w[:2]] if q!=w)
            assert competitor>=0
            pairs.append((log2(v/n),log2((n-v+alpha)/(competitor+alpha))))
        if len(pairs)<100:
            continue
        x,y=zip(*pairs)
        xc,yc=mean(x),mean(y)
        denom=sum((a-xc)**2 for a in x)
        if denom:
            classes[str(length)]=dict(types=len(pairs),information_mean=yc,
                                 slope=sum((a-xc)*(b-yc) for a,b in pairs)/denom)
    return classes

def main():
    cli=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    cli.add_argument('readings',type=Path)
    cli.add_argument('results',type=Path)
    args=cli.parse_args()
    r=json.loads(args.results.read_text())
    validated=0
    maximum=0.
    for name,record in r['works'].items():
        path=args.readings/r['inputs'][name]['file']
        tokens=path.read_text().split()
        for length, row in record.items():
            for alpha,observed in row['plain'].items():
                expected=prior_formula(tokens[:int(length)],float(alpha))
                assert len(expected)==observed['supported_bins']
                for word_size,by_size in expected.items():
                    validated+=1
                    for k,value in by_size.items():
                        e=abs(value-observed['per_length'][word_size][k])
                        maximum=max(maximum,e)
                        assert e<1e-12
    caesar=args.readings/r['inputs']['caesar']['file']
    raw=' '.join(caesar.read_text().split()[:30000])
    fixed=normalize(raw,'latin').split()
    threshold=r['calibration']['latin']['threshold']
    i=sorted(r['inputs']).index('caesar')
    fixed_scores=compare(fixed,30000,threshold,328115+1007*i)
    print(json.dumps(dict(groups_checked=validated,max_abs_error=maximum,
        caesar_latin_donor_normalization=dict(v_letter_instances=raw.count('v'),j_letter_instances=raw.count('j'),
        tokens=len(fixed),fixed_1={k:v['1'] for k,v in fixed_scores.items()})),indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':
    main()

"""Derive bounded historical word streams from public pinned source bytes."""
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
import json
import re
import subprocess
import unicodedata
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
TEI = "{http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0}"
TRANSLITERATE = str.maketrans({"œ": "oe", "æ": "ae", "þ": "th", "ð": "th", "ȝ": "gh"})


def digest(data):
    return sha256(data).hexdigest()


def normalize(text):
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text.casefold().translate(TRANSLITERATE))
    stripped = "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    return re.findall(r"[a-z]+", stripped)


def gower(text):
    opening = "Of hem that writen ous tofore"
    body = opening + text.split("\n" + opening, 1)[1].split("[End of CONFESSIO AMANTIS]", 1)[0]
    body = re.sub(r"_[^_]*_", "", body, flags=re.S)
    body = re.sub(r"\[[^\[\]]*\]", "", body, flags=re.S)
    return "\n".join(line for line in body.splitlines()
                     if not re.match(r"^\s*(?:Incipit|Explicit)\s", line))


def malory(text):
    body = text.split("\nBOOK I.\n", 1)[1]
    body = body.split("\nEnd of the Project Gutenberg EBook", 1)[0]
    return "\n".join(block for block in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", body)
                     if not re.match(r"\s*(?:CHAPTER|BOOK)\s+[IVXLCDM]+\.", block))


def caesar(text):
    xml = ET.fromstring(text)
    books = xml.findall(f".//{TEI}div[@subtype='book']")
    assert [book.get("n") for book in books] == list(map(str, range(1, 9)))
    return "\n".join("".join(p.itertext()) for book in books[:7] for p in book.iter(f"{TEI}p"))


def juan_manuel(text):
    opening = "Acaesció una vez, que el conde Lucanor estaba fablando en su poridad"
    body = opening + text.split(opening, 1)[1].split("\nEJEMPLO LI\n", 1)[0]
    kept = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", body):
        if re.match(r"^\s*(?:\[\d+\]|(?:ENXEMPLO|EXEMPLO|ENJIEMPLO|EJEMPLO)\s+[IVXLCDM]+\s*$)", block):
            continue
        kept.append(re.sub(r"\[\d+\]", "", block))
    return "\n".join(kept)


def llull(text):
    assert text.startswith("Senyor Deus gloriós")
    assert "Acabat es lo romanç de Evast e Blanquerna" in text[-500:]
    return text


def villani(text):
    opening = "Esaminando nell’animo la vostra esortazione"
    body = opening + text.split(opening, 1)[1].split("\nTAVOLA DEI CAPITOLI\n", 1)[0]
    body = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*(?:CAP\. (?:[IVXLCDM]+)\.|CAPITOLO PRIMO|LIBRO SECONDO)\s*$", "", body)
    body = re.sub(r"(?m)^_[^_\n]*_\s*$", "", body)
    return body


def boccaccio(text):
    opening = "[2] Umana cosa è aver compassione degli afflitti"
    ending = "[30] Qui finisce la Decima e ultima giornata"
    assert text.count(opening) == text.count(ending) == 1
    body = opening + text.split(opening, 1)[1].split(ending, 1)[0]
    # The PDF repeats the section name at page boundaries.
    heading = re.compile(r"\s*(?:Proemio|[IVXLCDM]+ Giornata(?:\s*[–-]\s*.+)?|Conclusione dell’autore|\d+)\s*",
                         re.IGNORECASE)
    return "\n".join(line for line in body.splitlines() if not heading.fullmatch(line))

def main():
    results = {}
    for ident, meta in WORKS.items():
        path = ROOT / meta["raw_file"]
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        assert digest(raw) == meta["raw_sha256"], ident
        if path.suffix == ".pdf":
            raw = subprocess.check_output(["pdftotext", "-enc", "UTF-8", "-nopgbrk", str(path), "-"])
            assert digest(raw) == meta["pdf_text_sha256"], ident
        body = globals()[ident](raw.decode("utf-8-sig").replace("\r\n", "\n"))
        words = normalize(body)
        assert len(words) >= 30_000, (ident, len(words))
        filename = ident + ".txt"
        tokens = (" ".join(words) + "\n").encode()
        (ROOT / filename).write_bytes(tokens)
        results[ident] = {**meta, "file": filename, "raw_bytes": path.stat().st_size,
                          "tokens": len(words), "sha256": digest(tokens)}
    manifest = {
        "preprocessing": "Casefold, transliterate œ/æ/þ/ð/ȝ, NFKD, remove combining marks, then maximal contiguous ASCII a–z runs. UTF-8, one space between tokens and final LF.",
        "preprocessing_script_sha256": digest(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
        "works": results,
    }
    (ROOT / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
                                       encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
